t.1.176.2: Then, O king, the Pāṇḍavas saw on the road that great-souled Dvaipāyana, pure of soul and free from stain.
t.1.176.3: Having duly paid him honour and having been comforted by him, and being given leave at the end of the conversation, they set out for the abode of Drupada.
t.1.176.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, O Janamejaya, the Pāṇḍavas set out for the southern Pāñcālas, who were protected by King Drupada.
t.1.176.4: Gazing upon the delightful forests and lakes, and dwelling here and there along the way, the great chariot-warriors journeyed on slowly.
t.1.176.5: Devoted to the study of the Veda, pure, gentle and pleasant of speech, the delights of the Kurus reached the Pāñcālas in due course.
t.1.176.6: But the Pāṇḍavas, having seen that city and the encampment, then made their lodging in the workshop of a potter.
t.1.176.7: There they gathered alms, having adopted the brahmin's way of life, and no men anywhere recognized those heroes who had then arrived.
t.1.176.8: But Yajñasena's constant wish was, "May I give Kṛṣṇā to the diadem-wearing Pāṇḍava," and yet he does not reveal this.
t.1.176.9: Searching for the sons of Kuntī, O Janamejaya, the Pāñcāla king had a strong bow made that could not be bent, O Bhārata.
t.1.176.10: He also had an artificial device made that hung in the air, and together with that device the king had a golden target made as well.
t.1.176.11: "Whoever strings this bow and, with this strung bow, passing through the aperture, pierces the target with arrows, he shall win my daughter."
t.1.176.12: Thus King Drupada had it proclaimed on every side. Hearing that, O Bhārata, all the kings assembled there.
t.1.176.13: And the great-souled seers came, out of a desire to see the svayaṃvara, and the Kurus too, led by Duryodhana and accompanied by Karṇa, O king.
t.1.176.14: And illustrious brahmins came together from many lands. Those hosts of kings were honored by the great-souled Drupada.
t.1.176.16: To the northeast of the city, on a level and auspicious stretch of ground, the assembly enclosure shone forth, surrounded on all sides by mansions.
t.1.176.15: Then all the townspeople, with a roar like that of the churning ocean, reached Śiśumārapura, and those kings too settled there.
t.1.176.17: It was furnished with ramparts and a moat, adorned with gates and arched gateways, and covered on every side with a many-colored canopy.
t.1.176.18: It was filled with hundreds of floods of music from instruments, perfumed with the smoke of costly aloe-wood, sprinkled with sandal-water, and adorned with garlands of flowers.
t.1.176.19: It was hemmed in by well-built, lofty mansions, enclosed on every side, which resembled the peaks of Kailāsa and scraped the vault of the sky.
t.1.176.20: With mansions enclosed in lattices of gold and adorned with jewel-inlaid floors, with stairways easy to climb, and furnished with great seats and coverings.
t.1.176.21: with many mansions elegantly roofed, perfumed with the finest aloe-wood, white and clear as swans in colour, and fragrant for a full yojana around.
t.1.176.22: They had a hundred unobstructed doors, were adorned with couches and seats, and their walls were overlaid with many metals, so that they looked like the peaks of Himavat.
t.1.176.23: There, in pavilions of many kinds, all the kings, finely adorned, took their seats, vying with one another.
t.1.176.24: There they saw, seated, the lions among kings, illustrious and of great courage and prowess, adorned with dark aloe-wood.
t.1.176.26: And on costly platforms on every side sat the people of the city and the countryside, for the delight of beholding Kṛṣṇā.
t.1.176.25: Greatly gracious, devoted to the brahmins, protectors of their own kingdoms, and beloved of all the world for their well-performed and auspicious deeds.
t.1.176.27: The Pāṇḍavas sat down together with the brāhmaṇas themselves, beholding that unsurpassed splendor of the king of the Pāñcālas.
t.1.176.28: Then, O king, that assembly grew in splendour for many days, abounding in the bestowal of jewels and adorned by actors and dancers.
t.1.176.29: While the assembly was in progress, on the delightful sixteenth day, she, her limbs freshly bathed, finely clothed and adorned with every ornament,
t.1.176.31: Then the purohita of the Somakas, a pure brāhmaṇa versed in the mantras, spread the sacred grass around and, according to the rite, offered clarified butter into the fire.
t.1.176.30: Then, O bull among the Bharatas, Draupadī descended into the arena, holding the golden, richly adorned bowl meant for the hero.
t.1.176.33: When that assembly had been made silent, O lord of the people, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, standing there in the middle of the arena, spoke aloud in a voice deep as a thundercloud these gentle, meaningful and excellent words.
t.1.176.32: Having gratified the fire and had the brāhmaṇas pronounce blessings, he silenced all the musical instruments on every side.
t.1.176.34: Here is the bow, here the target, and here are the arrows; let all the kings hear my words: passing through the opening in the device, strike the target with five sky-going arrows.
t.1.176.35: He who shall accomplish this most difficult deed, and who is endowed with lineage, beauty and strength, his wife this my sister Kṛṣṇā shall become today; I do not speak falsely.
t.1.176.36: Having thus spoken to them, the son of Drupada afterwards said this to Draupadī, proclaiming those assembled kings by name, by lineage, and by deeds.
